note: 31 NEW tools evaluated (zero overlap with the 49 in rig-tools.json). Licenses verified via repo metadata/search receipts for every entry. KEY FINDING: no existing named tool estimates bind pose from skin weights on a static mesh -- that is an in-house build on top of pygltflib (see top-3 summary). If any of the 5 corrupt-IBM GLBs contain animation clips, DemBones SSDR (already cataloged) can recover bone transforms from the posed sequence.

summary.bind_pose_recovery_assessment: No existing named open-source tool estimates a bind pose from skin weights on a STATIC mesh -- confirmed by targeted search. The recovery must be built in-house (weighted-centroid joint regression, SMPL-regressor style) on top of pygltflib. Two accelerants: (a) if any corrupt-IBM GLB contains animation clips, DemBones SSDR (already cataloged, license unverified) solves bone transforms + weights from the posed sequence -- CHECK THE 5 GLBS FOR ANIMATIONS FIRST; (b) skeletor (quarantined, GPL-3.0) extracts curve skeletons from the mesh for the all-joints-at-origin model. MediaPipe Pose is a 30-minute experimental spike, not a plan.
summary.license_corrections: glTF-Transform is MIT (not Apache-2.0); FBX2glTF is BSD-3-Clause (not Apache-2.0); Instant Meshes is reported BSD-3-Clause by downstream vendors but upstream GitHub shows NOASSERTION -- re-verify LICENSE.txt before integrating.

top_3_for_blocked_models.bind_pose_recipe: weight-weighted vertex centroids -> joint centers -> bind world matrices (identity or bone-aligned rotation) -> IBM = inverse(bind) -> rewrite skin accessor -> glTF-Validator -> rest-pose render check. In-house code, ~150 lines on top of pygltflib.
top_3_for_blocked_models.name: pygltflib
top_3_for_blocked_models.why: The only tool that lets us perform inverse-bind-matrix surgery directly on the 5 corrupt-IBM GLBs. Detect garbage IBMs, compute replacements from an estimated bind pose, write back, validate. Without this there is no scriptable IBM-repair path at all.

top_3_for_blocked_models.first_try: probreg.bcpd (variational Bayesian CPD) for outfit fitting; fall back to FilterReg for speed on dense meshes.
top_3_for_blocked_models.name: probreg
top_3_for_blocked_models.why: MIT, pip-installable, and a strict superset of pycpd: BCPD/FilterReg give faster, more outlier-robust non-rigid registration for outfit-to-body weight transfer across different topologies, and for consolidating the 12-skin source model's parts onto a common body.

top_3_for_blocked_models.first_command: gltf-transform merge part*.glb combined.glb --merge-scenes && gltf-transform inspect combined.glb
top_3_for_blocked_models.name: glTF-Transform
top_3_for_blocked_models.why: MIT CLI that directly attacks the 12-skin multi-skin source model (merge --merge-scenes into one file, then join in Blender) and gives the whole pipeline weld/inspect/optimize/draco/meshopt stages after Blender export.

task: open-source rigging tool pull-in program, wave 3 (bind-pose recovery / registration / glTF surgery focus)

tools.description: Python library for reading, writing and editing GLB/glTF at the JSON accessor level. Enables direct inverseBindMatrices surgery: detect garbage IBMs (1e38 etc.), compute replacement IBMs from an estimated bind pose, rewrite the skin accessor, save. Zero native deps, pip-installable.
tools.license: MIT (verified via conda-forge feedstock + downstream third-party tables)
tools.name: pygltflib
tools.notes: TOP-3 PICK. This is the plumbing that makes bind-pose recovery implementable for the 5 corrupt-IBM models. Proposed recipe: (1) load GLB, read skin.joints + inverseBindMatrices; (2) flag matrices with non-finite/absurd values; (3) estimate joint centers as skin-weight-weighted vertex centroids (SMPL-regressor style, in-house); (4) build bind world matrices (identity rotation or bone-direction aligned), IBM = inverse(bind); (5) write back via pygltflib, validate with glTF-Validator, verify rest pose renders identically. If the skeleton's own node transforms are also garbage, fall back to full re-rig (UniRig/Puppeteer GPU lane or blender_autorig.py).

tools.description: pip-installable Python library implementing CPD, Extended CPD, Color CPD, FilterReg (CVPR 2019), Bayesian CPD (BCPD), GMMReg, Support Vector Registration, GMMTree -- rigid AND non-rigid, with an Open3D interface. A strict superset of pycpd (already cataloged): BCPD and FilterReg are faster and more robust than vanilla CPD for noisy outfit-to-body fitting.
tools.license: MIT (verified on repo README badge)
tools.name: probreg
tools.notes: TOP-3 PICK. Pipeline use: non-rigidly register an unrigged outfit mesh (or a multi-skin part) onto the rigged body surface, then transfer weights via Blender Data Transfer (POLYINTERP_NEAREST) or nearest-vertex mapping. BCPD is the recommended first algorithm to try (variational Bayesian = robust to outliers). Directly serves the different-topology weight-transfer problem and the 12-skin source model consolidation.

tools.description: glTF 2.0 SDK + CLI (Node.js). Commands: merge (combines multiple GLBs, has --merge-scenes flag), weld (dedup vertices), inspect (vertex counts, size breakdown), simplify, quantize, draco, meshopt, prune, dedup, join/flatten. Core API manages array indices/byte offsets automatically.
tools.license: MIT (verified via GitHub repo metadata receipts + npm package.json)
tools.name: glTF-Transform
tools.notes: TOP-3 PICK. Directly serves the 12-skin multi-skin source model: `gltf-transform merge` the parts into one scene, then join meshes + unify armatures in Blender. Also the best build-stage seam after Blender export: weld -> simplify -> quantize -> meshopt/draco, and `inspect` for per-model QA stats. Correction to wave-2-era assumption: license is MIT, not Apache-2.0.

tools.description: C++ library for 3D global registration: Super4PCS / 4PCS algorithms. Finds rigid alignment between point clouds with NO initial guess -- the complement to ICP/pycpd/probreg, which all need a decent starting pose. Ships a command-line demo app.
tools.license: Apache-2.0 (verified in doc/overview.md: 'free for commercial and research use')
tools.name: OpenGR
tools.notes: Use when the outfit mesh and body are in wildly different poses/orientations and local methods (ICP/CPD) would fall into local minima. Get a coarse global alignment with OpenGR first, then refine with probreg BCPD. C++ build required; use as external binary, not vendored.

tools.description: Uniform surface remeshing via Voronoi clustering (based on Valette/Chassery ACVD). pip-installable, PyVista-integrated (mesh.acvd.remesh(n)). Produces evenly-sized triangles -- Bone Heat and voxel skinning both behave far better on uniform tessellation than on long skinny triangles.
tools.license: MIT (verified via conda-forge feedstock)
tools.name: pyacvd
tools.notes: Pre-rig sanitation step: run pyacvd uniform remesh on messy triangulated scans before automatic weights. Cheaper and more predictable than full retopo when the topology is merely uneven rather than broken.

tools.description: Bruno Levy (Inria) geometry library: CVT remeshing, mesh_repair(), exact-predicate booleans, remove_internal_shells(), surface reconstruction, parameterization. Python bindings via pygeogram-ap (https://github.com/PozzettiAndrea/pygeogram, BSD-3, nanobind).
tools.license: BSD-3-Clause (verified on repo README badge + Graphite docs)
tools.name: Geogram (+ pygeogram-ap)
tools.notes: Strong Manifold complement: Geogram's mesh_repair() + remove_internal_shells() handles self-intersecting scan soup that boolean-union alone cannot. Exact arithmetic makes its booleans robust where float-based ones fail. Use as external process (CLI) or via pygeogram-ap.

tools.category: mesh repair (hole fill / remesh / smooth / decimate)
tools.description: The Polygon Mesh Processing Library (Sieger & Botsch): hole filling, isotropic remeshing, smoothing, decimation, curvature. Python bindings via pypmp (https://github.com/PozzettiAndrea/pypmp, MIT, nanobind). Successor lineage of OpenMesh/Surface_mesh.
tools.license: MIT (verified on repo README: 'allowing for both open-source and commercial usage')
tools.name: PMP library (+ pypmp)
tools.notes: Permissive one-stop mesh surgery kit. Hole filling + remeshing + smoothing in one MIT package covers most pre-rig sanitation without touching GPL MeshLab.

tools.description: RWTH Aachen halfedge mesh framework with pybind11 Python bindings tightly integrated with numpy. Decimation, smoothing, subdivision, hole filling, SDF queries. `pip install openmesh` (wheels) or conda-forge.
tools.license: BSD-3-Clause (verified via conda-forge feedstock; pip package 'openmesh')
tools.name: OpenMesh (Python bindings)
tools.notes: Lower-level than trimesh: use when custom per-vertex/per-halfedge repair logic is needed (e.g. targeted spike removal, boundary loop surgery) that trimesh's batch ops cannot express.

tools.description: Jakob et al. SIGGRAPH Asia 2015: interactive field-aligned quad-dominant remeshing. Converts messy triangulated scans into clean quads with controllable density and edge flow. Prebuilt Windows binary available; Linux builds from source. Python bindings: PyNanoInstantMeshes (https://github.com/vork/PyNanoInstantMeshes, BSD-3).
tools.license: BSD-3-Clause (reported by multiple downstream vendors; upstream LICENSE.txt is BSD-style but GitHub metadata shows NOASSERTION -- confirm on repo before integrating)
tools.name: Instant Meshes
tools.notes: Clean quad topology is the single biggest lever for Bone Heat success and sane weight painting. Heavier than QuadriFlow (already cataloged) but better edge flow. License: treat as BSD-3 per downstream evidence, but re-verify the upstream LICENSE.txt text before vendoring -- GitHub license detection is inconclusive.

tools.description: zeux's gltfpack CLI (in meshoptimizer repo, gltf/ dir): quantize, simplify, reorder, meshopt-compress GLBs. MIT with attribution request. Complements gltf-transform (which also wraps meshopt) -- gltfpack is the reference implementation.
tools.license: MIT (verified on repo README)
tools.name: gltfpack (meshoptimizer)
tools.notes: Post-repair delivery step: slim repaired GLBs back to game budgets. Note: gltfpack's MESHOPT_compression output needs the meshopt decoder in three.js; prefer plain quantize+simplify for maximum engine compatibility.

tools.description: Official Khronos validator (Dart CLI + web + Node). Checks JSON schema, accessor bounds, skin/joint references, extension usage. Catches malformed skins (e.g. joint index out of range, IBM accessor count != joint count) that silently explode in viewers.
tools.license: Apache-2.0 (verified via multiple downstream THIRD_PARTY notices)
tools.name: glTF-Validator
tools.notes: Add to the repair pipeline as an automated gate: every repaired GLB must validate clean before it counts as fixed. Especially valuable for the IBM-surgery lane -- validates that rewritten skins are structurally sound.

tools.description: Python bindings for the Open Asset Import Library: reads 40+ 3D formats (FBX, DAE, OBJ, Blend, 3DS...) into one hierarchical structure with configurable post-processing (normal/tangent generation, triangulation, optimization). pip/conda installable.
tools.license: ISC for the Python bindings (verified via conda-forge feedstock); assimp core is BSD-3-Clause (verified on repo README)
tools.name: pyassimp
tools.notes: Useful if any blocked model needs to round-trip through a non-glTF format (e.g. FBX for a DCC tool that mangles GLB skins), or to cross-check a suspect GLB by re-importing it through an independent loader. Not a repair tool per se -- a format escape hatch.

tools.description: Facebook's FBX-to-glTF converter. Preserves skins, blend shapes and animations through the conversion. CLI binary.
tools.license: BSD-3-Clause (verified on repo README; not Apache as sometimes assumed)
tools.name: FBX2glTF
tools.notes: Escape hatch for the corrupt-IBM models: if a model exists in FBX form anywhere (source asset, backup), converting with FBX2glTF may produce a clean skin where the GLB exporter wrote garbage IBMs. Worth checking whether FBX originals exist for the 5 blocked models.

tools.description: Cython Python wrapper for Google Draco: encode/decode meshes and point clouds from numpy. pip-installable wheels. Use for KHR_draco_mesh_compression round-trips in Python without Node.
tools.license: Apache-2.0 (verified; Google Draco core is also Apache-2.0)
tools.name: DracoPy
tools.notes: Delivery-side only (smaller downloads). Note the pygfx caveat: DracoPy historically covered positions/normals/UVs/colors but not all glTF attributes -- verify skin attributes (JOINTS/WEIGHTS) survive a DracoPy round-trip before using on rigged models.

tools.description: Microsoft's older glTF CLI: GLB<->glTF conversion, Draco compression, asset optimization for realtime use. Windows-centric, last updated ~2021, but MIT and functional.
tools.license: MIT (verified on repo README)
tools.name: glTF-Toolkit (Microsoft)
tools.notes: Superseded in practice by gltf-transform for most tasks; kept as a fallback converter if a file trips gltf-transform's parser. Low priority.

tools.description: Cesium's Node.js glTF pipeline: glTF<->GLB conversion, embed/separate buffers and textures, glTF 1.0->2.0 upgrade, Draco compression. CLI + library.
tools.license: Apache-2.0 (verified on repo README badge)
tools.name: gltf-pipeline (CesiumGS)
tools.notes: The buffer/texture embed-separate controls are handy when hand-editing a GLB's skin section: convert GLB->gltf+bin, edit JSON (e.g. inspect IBM accessor), convert back. Pairs with pygltflib workflows.

tools.description: BlazePose-based 33-landmark 3D human pose estimation from a single image, CPU-realtime, pip-installable. Experimental application: render the corrupt-IBM model from front/side views in its rest pose, run Pose Landmarker, triangulate the 3D landmarks into joint-center estimates, use as the bind-pose seed for IBM reconstruction.
tools.license: Apache-2.0 (verified; Pose Landmarker models also Apache-2.0 per model card)
tools.name: MediaPipe Pose (Google)
tools.notes: EXPERIMENTAL, flagged honestly: BlazePose is trained on photos of real humans, not 3D renders of stylized characters -- accuracy on our models is unproven. But it is Apache-2.0, runs on CPU in seconds, and gives an independent joint-position estimate to cross-check against the weight-centroid method. Worth a 30-minute spike on one blocked model; do not build the pipeline on it until the spike validates.

tools.description: Ships with Blender 4.0.2: Analyze finds non-manifold edges, bad contiguous edges, intersecting faces, zero-area faces, thin walls; Clean Up offers Make Manifold, merge distance, fill holes. Fully scriptable headless (bpy.ops.mesh.print3d_*).
tools.license: GPL (bundled with Blender; tool use fine, outputs are ours)
tools.name: Blender 3D-Print Toolbox (built-in)
tools.notes: Zero-install pre-rig QA: run the analysis headless on every blocked model, log defect counts, and only then choose the repair tool (trimesh/Manifold/Geogram). Gives the 'before' numbers for side-by-side proof.

tools.description: Projects outfit mesh vertices onto the body surface (nearest-surface-point mode) before weight transfer. Headless-scriptable. The standard trick for making non-conforming garments follow the body so Data Transfer weights land on the right bones.
tools.license: GPL (bundled with Blender; tool use fine)
tools.name: Blender Shrinkwrap modifier (built-in)
tools.notes: Pipeline: shrinkwrap outfit to body -> Blender Data Transfer (POLYINTERP_NEAREST) weights -> optional probreg BCPD pre-alignment for large pose gaps. Cheaper than full non-rigid registration when the outfit is already roughly placed.

tools.category: weight transfer between different topologies (cage binding)
tools.description: Mesh Deform binds the outfit to a low-res cage of the BODY (not the skeleton); Surface Deform binds to the body surface itself. Transfer path: bind body to cage -> bind outfit to same cage -> bake body weights through cage to outfit. Handles topology differences without any correspondence search.
tools.license: GPL (bundled with Blender; tool use fine)
tools.name: Blender Mesh Deform / Surface Deform modifiers (built-in)
tools.notes: Alternative to pycpd/probreg when registration is unstable: no point-correspondence needed, just a cage. Mesh Deform is the more robust of the two for bulky outfits (armor, jackets); Surface Deform for skin-tight clothing.

tools.description: Armature modifier 'Preserve Volume' switches deformation from linear blend skinning to dual-quaternion skinning, which eliminates the candy-wrapper collapse at elbows/knees that bad weights exaggerate. Scriptable; bakes to shape keys for export if the engine needs LBS.
tools.license: GPL (bundled with Blender; tool use fine)
tools.name: Blender Dual-Quaternion Preserve Volume (built-in)
tools.notes: Not a weight fix -- a deformation fix that makes imperfect weights shippable. For weight bleed at twist joints (forearm, thigh), DQS + modest weight smoothing often beats chasing perfect weights. Verify the target engine supports DQS or bake the result.

tools.description: bpy.ops.object.vertex_group_mirror / Symmetrize copies weights from the good side to the broken side across the X axis, with topology or nearest-vertex matching. Scriptable headless.
tools.license: GPL (bundled with Blender; tool use fine)
tools.name: Blender Symmetrize vertex groups (built-in)
tools.notes: Weight bleed is very often asymmetric (one bad armpit, one bad hip). Fix the good side once (manually or via smoothing), symmetrize, done. Combine with Limit Total (4 influences) + Normalize All in the same headless pass.

tools.category: auto-skinning reference (bounded biharmonic weights) + mesh repair
tools.description: Alec Jacobson et al. geometry processing library: the REFERENCE implementation of Bounded Biharmonic Weights (Jacobson et al. 2011) -- the industry-standard smooth weight solver -- plus booleans, winding numbers, signed distances, ARAP, LSCM. Python bindings via the 'igl' pip package (subset of functions).
tools.license: MPL-2.0 (verified on repo README: 'primarily MPL2 licensed'; some files carry other licenses)
tools.name: libigl
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (weak copyleft MPL-2.0: file-level; usable as an unmodified library but not vendored/copied into our MIT tree without review). BBW is the 'smarter than proximity' weight solver we want: smooth, shape-aware, sparsity-encouraging. Practical path: pip install igl, call igl.bbw on a tetrahedralized mesh (needs tetgen/fTetWild step -- fragile on messy meshes, per the hiho-software research note), export weights, import into Blender. The 2024 'Robust Biharmonic Skinning Using Geometric Fields' (MIT/USC) paper removes the tet-meshing requirement but has NO public code -- clean-room reimplementation is a larger project.

tools.description: Inria surface+volume remesher (mmgs/mmg3d/mmg2d): anisotropic adaptation, isotropic remeshing, implicit-domain meshing. Strong on CAD-like and dense meshes.
tools.license: LGPL (verified on repo README + mmgtools.org docs)
tools.name: MMG (MmgTools)
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (LGPL: evaluate ideas only, do not integrate). Capabilities overlap pyacvd (MIT) and Geogram (BSD-3) for our surface-remesh needs; no unique must-have for character repair.

tools.category: mesh repair (full MeshLab filter suite, Python)
tools.description: Python bindings for MeshLab: 300+ filters -- isotropic remeshing, Poisson/ball-pivoting reconstruction, ambient occlusion, decimation, hole filling, curvature. pip wheels available.
tools.license: GPL-3.0 (verified in setup.py license='GPL3' + multiple third-party notices)
tools.name: pymeshlab
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (GPL-3.0: install-as-tool only, never vendor; outputs are ours). The most complete repair toolbox available -- but trimesh + Manifold + Geogram cover our needs permissively. Note: RigAnything's pipeline depends on pymeshlab, which is one more reason that project is unusable for us.

tools.category: mesh repair (alpha wrap / booleans / isotropic remesh / self-intersection repair)
tools.description: The Computational Geometry Algorithms Library: Polygon Mesh Processing package does isotropic remeshing, hole filling, alpha wrapping (shrink-wrap any soup into a watertight mesh), corefinement booleans, self-intersection repair. SWIG Python/Java bindings exist.
tools.license: GPL-3.0 / LGPL-3.0 dual (verified: algorithms GPL-3.0, kernel/support LGPL-3.0; commercial licenses from GeometryFactory)
tools.name: CGAL
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (GPL-3.0 on the algorithms we would use). Alpha Wrap is the standout: it can turn the worst mesh soup into a watertight solid, which is exactly the Bone-Heat-unblocker use case. If a blocked model defeats Manifold+Geogram+trimesh, CGAL Alpha Wrap as an external binary is the escalation path -- but keep it out of the integrated pipeline.

tools.description: navis-org skeleton extraction: mesh contraction (Au et al. 2008), wavefront, vertex clusters, edge collapse, TEASAR. Pure Python + numpy/scipy, pip-installable. Outputs node positions, parent edges, radii, mesh->skeleton map.
tools.license: GPL-3.0 (verified in source-file license headers)
tools.name: skeletor
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (GPL-3.0: run as external tool, do not vendor). Directly relevant to the 1 model with NO skeleton transforms (all joints at origin): extract a curve skeleton from the mesh, snap it to anatomical joint positions, build the armature from it. Also useful as a joint-position cross-check for the 5 corrupt-IBM models. TEASAR needs a watertight-ish mesh -- repair first.

tools.description: Community continuation of ManuelBastioniLAB: parametric photorealistic humanoid generator inside Blender (age/mass/tone sliders), ships with its own rigged base meshes.
tools.license: AGPL-3.0 (verified via Wikipedia + project docs; assets are CC-BY)
tools.name: MB-Lab
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (AGPL-3.0: evaluate only). Not a repair tool for existing models, but its rigged base meshes could serve as anatomical proportion references for rebuilding the all-joints-at-origin model. Blender 4.0+ community builds exist.

tools.description: 15+ year parametric humanoid generator: body/face parameters, clothing/hair assets, exports OBJ/FBX/DAE with full skeletons. Source is AGPL; everything it exports is CC0 (explicit project exception).
tools.license: AGPL-3.0 for source code (verified via project license page); CORE ASSETS AND EXPORTED MODELS ARE CC0
tools.name: MakeHuman
tools.notes: QUARANTINE the application (AGPL), but NOTE THE CC0 ESCAPE HATCH: meshes+rigs exported from an unmodified MakeHuman binary are CC0 and can be used freely -- e.g. as a clean reference skeleton to retarget/rebuild a blocked model against. Same split applies to MPFB2 (https://github.com/makehumancommunity/mpfb2, GPL-3.0 code / CC0 assets), the modern Blender 4.x addon.

tools.description: Modern MakeHuman frontend as a Blender addon: same parametric bodies, direct in-Blender manipulation, all Blender export formats. Code GPL-3.0, assets/outputs CC0.
tools.license: GPL-3.0 for source code (verified via MakeHuman community license page); assets CC0
tools.name: MPFB2
tools.notes: QUARANTINE (GPL-3.0: tool-use only). Same CC0-export escape hatch as MakeHuman. More practical than standalone MakeHuman since it runs inside our Blender 4.0.2.

tools.description: Adobe Research template-free autoregressive rigging: predicts skeletons AND skinning weights for arbitrary meshes, inference scripts take .glb/.obj and export a rigged GLB. Checkpoints on HuggingFace.
tools.license: Research-only (third-party assessment; repo carries a custom LICENSE.md, no OSI permissive license found)
tools.name: RigAnything (Isabella98Liu, SIGGRAPH TOG 2025)
tools.notes: REJECTED: research-only license (not integrable per rules), needs GPU (blocked on this VM like UniRig/Puppeteer), and its pipeline depends on pymeshlab (GPL-3.0). Interesting only as architecture reference. UniRig / Puppeteer / MagicArticulate (already cataloged, Apache-2.0/MIT) remain the GPU-lane options.
